name: es30-skybox-and-fog
title: Skybox, environment mapping and fog
summary: An outdoor scene around one CPU-painted cube map (sky gradient, sun, two mountain ranges): a skybox drawn last with the .xyww depth trick and LEQUAL, a chrome sphere and a gold box with reflect(), a glass sphere with refract() and the Fresnel-Schlick blend, and a checkered ground that dissolves into exponential-squared fog. Validated in a NEAREST configuration against a CPU ray caster with ES 3.0 Table 3.21 face selection and the GLSL ES 3.00 reflect/refract formulas (21 per-object sweeps, one of them on a close-up of the glass sphere), plus six face-direction probes with a face-coded cube map, seamless LINEAR lookups exactly on cube edges, a fog blend at a known distance and negative controls (swapped faces, mirrored face models, inverse eta, no Fresnel, depth trick off, fog off).
spec: ES 3.0 §3.8.9 Cube Map Texture Selection and Table 3.21 (major axis, sc/tc/ma, s = (sc/|ma| + 1)/2; ties are implementation-defined)
ES 3.0 §3.8.9.1 Seamless Cube Map Filtering (wrap modes ignored; NEAREST clamps to edge; LINEAR takes border texels from the neighbouring face) and Appendix F.2 (behaviour change from ES 2.0)
ES 3.0 §3.8.10.2 Coordinate Wrapping and Texel Selection (NEAREST texel; LINEAR weights alpha = frac(u - 1/2))
ES 3.0 §3.8.4 Immutable-Format Texture Images (TexStorage2D with TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP), §3.8.5 Alternate Texture Image Specification Commands (TexSubImage2D per face target)
ES 3.0 §2.13 Coordinate Transformations and §2.13.1 Controlling the Viewport (z_d = z_c / w_c, z_w = (f - n)/2 z_d + (n + f)/2), §2.18 Primitive Clipping (-w_c <= z_c <= w_c)
ES 3.0 §4.1.5 Depth Buffer Test (LESS / LEQUAL), §4.2.3 Clearing the Buffers (ClearDepthf)
ES 3.0 §2.1.6.2 Conversion from Floating-Point to Normalized Fixed-Point (8-bit result is one of the two closest values)
GLSL ES 3.00 §8.5 Geometric Functions (reflect, refract incl. the k < 0 case, normalize, dot, length)
GLSL ES 3.00 §8.8 Texture Lookup Functions (texture with samplerCube), §4.1.7 Samplers
GLSL ES 3.00 §8.2 Exponential Functions (exp), §8.3 Common Functions (mix, clamp, floor, mod), §4.5.1 Range and Precision

api.glGenTextures: three cube maps (sky, face-coded, seam test) plus a temporary swapped-face cube map in validate()
api.glBindTexture: TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP on unit 0; TEXTURE_BINDING_CUBE_MAP reads back the sky texture while the scene is drawn; switching to the face-coded texture changes every environment lookup as the CPU model predicts
api.glActiveTexture: TEXTURE0, the unit every samplerCube uniform is set to; all lookups match the CPU model of the bound cube map
api.glTexStorage2D: TEXTURE_CUBE_MAP, RGBA8, 10 levels of 512^2 (sky), 1 level of 5^2 and 2^2; sampled texels equal the uploaded ones
api.glTexSubImage2D: one upload per face target POSITIVE_X..NEGATIVE_Z: looking along each axis the screen centre shows the centre texel of that target's image and 81 probes per face match Table 3.21; uploading the +X and -X images to each other's targets makes every +X probe fail the correct model and match the swapped one
api.glTexParameteri: MIN/MAG_FILTER NEAREST (read back; exact texels) and LINEAR (50/50 average across cube edges); WRAP_S/T = REPEAT on the seam texture is ignored for cube maps as ES 3.0 3.8.9.1 requires
api.glGetTexParameteriv: TEXTURE_MIN_FILTER and TEXTURE_MAG_FILTER of the sky cube map read back NEAREST in the validation configuration
api.glGetIntegerv: TEXTURE_BINDING_CUBE_MAP and MAX_CUBE_MAP_TEXTURE_SIZE (>= the 512 face size)
api.glDeleteTextures: the temporary swapped cube map in validate() and the three cube maps in shutdown(); final glGetError == NO_ERROR
api.glEnable: DEPTH_TEST: objects drawn before the sky stay in front of it (probes on all three objects)
api.glDepthFunc: LESS for the scene, LEQUAL for the sky at window depth 1.0: sky pixels pass against the cleared 1.0 everywhere nothing was drawn (sky sweeps), objects survive; with the depth trick removed the sky cube covers the whole scene
api.glClearDepthf: 1.0, the value the sky's depth (z_d = w/w = 1) must pass with LEQUAL
api.glClear: COLOR | DEPTH before every frame; 15 consecutive frames drawn by validate() each match their own CPU reference
api.glViewport: full surface for the scene (CPU-projected probes land on the predicted pixels at 256x256, 800x800, 640x480, 333x777, 1280x400) and a 4x4 viewport for the seam probes
api.glGetUniformLocation: all uniforms of the three programs; the uploaded values reach the shaders (every sweep matches)
api.glUniform1i: samplerCube units, u_material (ground / mirror / glass) and the bool u_depth_trick (false = negative control)
api.glUniform1f: u_eta (1/1.5 matches, 1.5 is rejected at 151 discriminating glass pixels and matches its own model), u_fog_density (sqrt(ln 2)/d gives the 50/50 blend; 0 gives the unfogged colour), u_f0, u_tile
api.glUniform3f: eye, tints, fog colour, sun, albedos and the probe direction (exact cube-edge directions)
api.glUniformMatrix4fv: u_model / u_view / u_proj and the skybox view (rotation only via mat3(u_view)) and projection: sky directions and object pixels agree with the CPU camera
api.glGenVertexArrays: one VAO per mesh (ground grid, 128 x 64 sphere, cube shared by the gold box and the skybox)
api.glBindVertexArray: per draw; VAO 0 for the attribute-less probe triangle
api.glGenBuffers: vertex and index buffer per mesh
api.glBindBuffer: ARRAY_BUFFER and ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER (bound while the VAO is bound)
api.glBufferData: interleaved position + normal floats and uint16 indices; observed through the geometry and the normals of every object
api.glVertexAttribPointer: interleaved layout; the normals drive reflect/refract and match the analytic sphere and box normals
api.glDrawElements: TRIANGLES with UNSIGNED_SHORT indices for the ground, spheres, box and skybox
api.glDrawArrays: one attribute-less TRIANGLES draw (positions from gl_VertexID) per seam probe
api.glReadPixels: whole-frame and single-pixel RGBA8 readback for every comparison
api.glGetError: drained after validation and after shutdown: NO_ERROR

visual_review.notes: Viewed the CTest captures gpu es-max and llvmpipe es-min (256x256, identical to the eye) and own captures at 800x600, 333x777, 1280x400 (zink es-min) and an orbited frame at t = 15 s. Blue sky graded to a pale haze at the horizon, a sun disc with a warm glow top left, two smooth anti-aliased mountain silhouettes (pale far range, darker near range), a bright haze band where the fogged ground meets the sky, and a green checkered ground losing contrast with distance. Left a chrome sphere reflecting the blue zenith above and the hazy ground below, centre a gold box with tinted flat-mirror faces, right a glass sphere showing the inverted sky with a bright reflective rim. No seam is visible along the cube edges in the 1280x400 view (horizontal half-angle 56 degrees). Portrait and wide captures fill the surface with all three objects in view.
